rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When waw coordinates with the sense ‘with’ onto a nominative-only construction, the following noun takes the same nominative role as its antecedent.
rows.anchor: لأن الواو فى المعنيين جميعا يعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You and your business’ reports a present state and stays nominative; waw can also join two subjects under a shared predicate.
rows.anchor: وأما أنت وشأنك وكل امرئ وضيعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنت أعلم وعبد الله can mean ‘you are more knowledgeable with Abdullah’; alternatively, you and Abdullah are both subjects of ‘more knowledgeable.’
rows.anchor: وأنت أعلم وعبد الله أى أنت أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما أنت and كيف أنت act as nominal beginnings, so nouns joined after them with the sense ‘with’ remain nominative; this differs from a verb such as صنعت.
rows.anchor: ما أنت وما زيد فيحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line attributed to Ziyād al-Aʿjam (or another poet) shows waw meaning ‘with’ while the following noun is nominative.
rows.anchor: يدلك على ذلك قول الشاعر وهو زياد الأعجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs’ expression إنك ما وخيرا means إنك مع خير, confirming maʿa as the conjunction’s sense.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك قول العرب إنك ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAntara’s line coordinates Jarwa with the speaker in the nominative, since إني functions as a nominal beginning rather than a verb.
rows.anchor: وقال وهو لأبى عنترة العبسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative after ما أنت or كيف أنت is not a regular construction; it would require treating a nonverbal expression like a verb.
rows.anchor: ولم نر شيئا من هذا ليس بفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs rarely say كيف أنت وزيدا or ما أنت وزيدا; Sībawayh explains the accusative through an understood تكون or كنت.
rows.anchor: وزعموا أن ناسا يقولون كيف أنت وزيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted كنت or تكون is recoverable because those verbs commonly occur in these ‘with’ constructions and preserve their intended meaning.
rows.anchor: كأنه قال كيف تكون أنت وقصعة من ثريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In present-state expressions such as أنت وشأنك, speakers do not use كان or يكون; they build the utterance directly on the nominal beginning.
rows.anchor: لا يريد كان ولا يكون

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب
rows.claim: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reports that trusted Arabs recited أتوعدني بقومك with accusative, reflecting an understood verbal construction.
rows.anchor: وزعم أبو الخطاب أنه سمع بعض العرب

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: Al-Rāʿī reportedly recited أزمان قومي والجماعة with accusative, construed with an elided كان because the event is past.
rows.anchor: وزعموا أن الراعى كان ينشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣirma al-Anṣārī’s verse illustrates carrying a phrase on a frequent underlying verbal construction, as with لست بمدرك.
rows.anchor: وهذا مشبه بقول صرمة الأنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Akhwaṣ’s line is carried on ليسوا بمصلحين, showing how an understood verbal phrase supplies the construction.
rows.anchor: ليسوا بمصلحين ولست بمدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀmir ibn Juwayn al-Ṭāʾī’s line reflects an understood أن, which poets often use here under metrical pressure.
rows.anchor: لأن الشعراء قد يستعملون أن ههنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For three-consonant nouns on the فَعْل pattern, the small-count plural through ten is normally أفعل.
rows.anchor: أما ما كان من الأسماء على ثلاثة أحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Above ten, this noun class commonly forms plurals on فعال or فعول.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاوز العدد هذا فإن البناء قد يجئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some nouns allow both فعول and فعال, while فعيل plurals such as الكليب and العبيد are rare.
rows.anchor: فقالوا فعول وفعال وذلك قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفعال sometimes replaces أفعل in this class; the cited al-Aʿshā line witnesses أزناد.
rows.anchor: يجئ في فعل أفعال مكان أفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A plural on فعلة occurs as a nonbasic alternative, as in جبء/جبأة, فقع/فقعة, and قعب/قعبة.
rows.anchor: وربما كسر الفعل على فعلة كما كسر على فعال

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Khalīl explains forms such as الفحالة and البعولة as adding feminine marking; other patterns are learned by transmission and analogy.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل أنهم إنما أرادوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خمسة كلاب can mean five individual members of the dog kind, like using كلاب for a dog's sound or رمان for its seed.
rows.anchor: وقد يجئ خمسة كلاب يراد به خمسة من الكلاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three-letter nouns on the فَعَل pattern take أفعال for small counts.
rows.anchor: وما كان على ثلاثة أحرف وكان فعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For larger counts in that class, فعال is more common than فعول; other nouns use فعلان forms.
rows.anchor: فأما الفعال فنحو جمال وجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An أفعال form can serve for larger numbers too, making a separate high-count pattern unnecessary, as with أقتاب and أرسان.
rows.anchor: يستغنى به أن يكسر الاسم على البناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak-final nouns generally follow the same plural patterns, though particular forms and limits depend on attested usage.
rows.anchor: وبنات الياء والواو تجري هذا المجرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doubled nouns likewise use أفعال forms such as ألباب and أمداد; this may be their only attested plural pattern.
rows.anchor: وتقول في المضاعف لبب وألباب ومدد وأمداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For another uncommon three-letter pattern, the small-count plural is أفعال; its low frequency limits extension to other patterns.
rows.anchor: وما كان على ثلاثة أحرف وكان فعلا فإنما تكسره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms such as النمور and الوعول are rare analogies to الأسود rather than the regular pattern for this class.
rows.anchor: وهذا النحو قليل فلما جاز لهم أن يثبتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs say ثلاثة قروء in place of the expected small-count form ثلاثة أقرؤ; this is the plural form used in the verse.
rows.anchor: ثلاثة قروء فاستغنوا بها عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some nouns use a feminine-ended plural such as قردة for a small count instead of the expected form أقراد.
rows.anchor: وقد يكسر على فعلة نحو قرد وقردة وحسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another three-consonant class takes أفعال for small counts and often فعول or فعال for larger counts, with فعول more frequent.
rows.anchor: فإنه إذا كسر على ما يكون

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Khalīl analyzes الفلك as masculine in the singular and feminine in the plural, citing two Qur'anic usages as evidence.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الخليل ومثله رهن ورهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For nouns on فعلة such as قصعة, small counts take the feminine suffix with fatḥa; larger counts usually use فعال.
rows.anchor: أما ما كان على فعلة فإنك إذا أردت أدنى العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The larger-count pattern for that class is فعال, though some nouns instead form plurals on فعول.
rows.anchor: فعال وذلك قصعة وقصاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine suffix can also denote a large number, as Ḥassān ibn Thābit’s الجفنات line shows.
rows.anchor: وقد يجمعون بالتاء وهم يريدون الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak-final nouns in this class follow the same patterns, including forms in ركوة and قشوة.
rows.anchor: بتلك المنزلة تقول ركوة وركاء وركوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another feminine noun pattern has both a suffixed small-count form and a larger broken plural, as in رحبات and رحاب.
rows.anchor: وأما ما كان فعلة فهو في أدنى العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nouns on فعلة take a suffixed plural with ḍamma on the middle consonant for small counts, then commonly a broken plural on فعل.
rows.anchor: وأما ما كانت فعلة فإنك إذا كسرته على بناء أدنى العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some nouns of that class also form larger-count plurals on فعال; dialects may open the middle vowel in the suffixed plural.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك نقرة ونقار وبرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited line attests the dialectal opening of the middle vowel in this plural.
rows.anchor: ومن العرب من يفتح العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak-final wāw nouns use parallel suffixed and broken plurals, as in خطوة/خطوات/خطى and عروة/عروات/عرى.
rows.anchor: وبنات الواو بهذه المنزلة قالوا خطوة وخطوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak-final yāʾ nouns often use the larger-count form without the feminine suffix, avoiding yāʾ after ḍamma.
rows.anchor: بنات الياء إذا كسرت على بناء الأكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A plural may be used directly after a numeral without a feminine numeral form, as in ثلاث غرف and ركب.
rows.anchor: وقد يقولون ثلاث غرف وركب وأشباه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Geminated nouns pattern like ركبة; their doubled consonant stays intact in forms such as سرر and جدد.
rows.anchor: والمضاعف بمنزلة ركبة قالوا سرات وسرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For feminine nouns on فعلة, small counts add the feminine suffix with kasra on the middle consonant; some dialects instead open it.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك قربات وسدرات وكسرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Larger-count forms are bare plurals such as سدر and قرب; speakers may use them for small numbers because this class rarely takes the suffix.
rows.anchor: ومن قال غرفات فخفف قال كسرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak-final yāʾ and wāw forms avoid the suffixed plural after kasra, as in لحية/لحى and فرية/فرى.
rows.anchor: تقول لحية ولحى وفرية وفرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doubled nouns in this class form both suffixed and broken plurals, as in قدة/قدات/قدد and ربة/ربات/ربب.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك قدة وقدات وقدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفعل plurals such as أنعم and أشد occur but are rare and nonbasic.
rows.anchor: وقد كسرت فعلة على أفعل وذلك قليل عزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the feminine suffix, some feminine nouns form plurals on فعل, as in تخمة/تخم and تهمة/تهم; this differs from masculine رطب.
rows.anchor: والفعلة تكسر على فعل إن لم تجمع بالتاء
